sections.title: Entry and documents
sections.body: EU citizens need only an ID card; everyone else needs a valid passport. Check if you require any specific travel insurance that covers skiing. Note that border checks may be in place, especially during peak seasons.

sections.title: What January is like in Val Gardena
sections.body: January is prime ski season in Val Gardena, with numerous thick snowfalls making for excellent skiing conditions. Expect cold temperatures, often ranging from -5°C to 5°C. The days are short, with daylight lasting about 8 to 9 hours, so layers and warm clothing are essential.

sections.title: How to pay in Val Gardena
sections.body: Cash is widely accepted, but many restaurants and shops also take credit cards. ATMs are plentiful in the area, so withdrawing cash for smaller vendors is wise. Plan for daily expenses of around €70-150 per person, especially if enjoying meals with wine.

sections.title: Getting in from the airport
sections.body: The nearest major airport is Bolzano, about an hour's drive away. You can take a ski shuttle or rent a car. Buses also service the area from larger hubs, like Innsbruck or Verona, with transfers available to Val Gardena.
bullets: Check bus services from Innsbruck or Verona

sections.title: Getting around Val Gardena
sections.body: Val Gardena is walkable, but buses and ski shuttles can take you between towns and ski lifts. Consider a Dolomiti Superski pass for unlimited access to several ski areas. Local buses run frequently, especially during the ski season.
bullets: Walking is a viable option for local travel

sections.title: Food and drink basics
sections.body: Dinner typically starts around 7 PM, with many restaurants serving hearty local options like speck and polenta. Lunch on the slopes sees a mixture of traditional food outlets and quick bites. Don't miss the chance to try local wines after your meal.
bullets: Look for speck and polenta dishes

sections.title: Personal safety while skiing
sections.body: Always wear a helmet when skiing and follow local safety guidelines on the slopes. Insurance that covers skiing and any potential mountain rescue is highly recommended. Be cautious of avalanche conditions and check reports daily.
bullets: Insurance that covers skiing is essential

sections.title: Tipping culture in restaurants
sections.body: Tipping is customary in Italy, usually around 10% if service is good. Check the bill for service charge as it might already be included. Leaving small change is seen as polite.
bullets: Round up to the next euro is common

sections.title: Packing specifics for skiing
sections.body: Pack warm layers, waterproof jackets, and essential skiing gear. Don't forget goggles and gloves. If you plan to rent gear, check local rental shops for advance bookings, especially during the busy season.
bullets: Goggles and gloves are a must

sections.title: Apps worth installing before landing
sections.body: Consider downloading local transport apps for bus schedules and ski area maps. Additionally, apps for weather forecasts can help you plan ski days effectively.
